content: Is there a reason IsNowhereDense has no union lemma while IsMeagre does?

I think so: using docs#IsNowhereDense.closure and docs#IsNowhereDense.mono you reduce to closed sets. Then, using docs#IsClosed.interior_union_left you get interior (s ∪ t) ⊆ s, hence interior (s ∪ t) ⊆ interior s = ∅.
it's true for finite unions but not always for infinite ones, I think
Rat is a countable union of nowhere dense singletons
In any case, @Mario Càllisto, this would be a good first contribution, if you're interested!

Thanks all. That proof is much shorter than what I had — I was going through Dense and Dense.inter_of_isOpen_left; reducing to closed sets and using IsClosed.interior_union_left is cleaner. I'll try opening a PR.
Once it's done you can post its number here, note that if you write #xxx where xxx is the PR number, Zulip transforms this into a clickable link.
